candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is Spindle Cell Hemangioma, a vascular neoplasm composed of cavernous vascular spaces and spindle cells. Giant Cell Tumor of bone is an osteoclast-rich neoplasm with multinucleated giant cells and stromal mononuclear cells — a fundamentally different diagnostic entity. While both can produce lytic frontal bone lesions with soft-tissue components on imaging, they are not equivalent and cannot be reconciled as aliases or variants of each other.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Giant Cell Tumor of bone is a distinct neoplastic entity from Spindle Cell Hemangioma; both can present as lytic skull lesions but differ in histology, cell of origin, and diagnostic classification

case_quality_flags: Spindle Cell Hemangioma of the frontal bone is an uncommon diagnosis; imaging features described (soap-bubble lytic lesion, cortical destruction, soft-tissue component, avid enhancement) are not pathognomonic and overlap with several other entities including Giant Cell Tumor, making histopathologic confirmation essential for definitive diagnosis.
